draft.title: Post-sentencing
card: Parole
Parole lets a prisoner serve the last part of a sentence in the community, under supervision. It is a release on conditions, and the sentence has not ended.
Conditions
A parolee must follow set conditions, such as reporting to a supervising officer. If they break the conditions, parole can be revoked and they may return to prison.
Parole decisions

In NSW, the State Parole Authority decides whether a prisoner is released on parole. The sentencing court sets the length of the sentence and any non-parole period, which is the minimum time to serve before parole can be considered.
After the sentence
Some serious offenders can be kept in custody or supervised in the community after their sentence ends. These orders aim to protect the community from a risk of serious harm.
draft.remember: Parole is release under supervision during a sentence. Post-sentence orders can apply once the sentence is over.

a.q: Which statement best describes a prisoner who is released on parole?
opts: They serve part of the sentence under community supervision
They have finished the sentence and have no conditions left
They have had the conviction overturned by a higher court
They have been given a lighter sentence by the judge
a.why: Parole is part of the sentence served in the community, with supervision and conditions. It is not the end of the sentence, so the option about having no conditions left is wrong.
a.clue: Is the sentence over when parole starts?

b.q: Sam is on parole. He stops reporting to his supervising officer, and the State Parole Authority revokes his parole. What is the most likely result?
opts: He may be returned to prison to serve more of the sentence
His conviction is quashed because he was supervised unfairly
His sentence is treated as finished because he was released
He is sent to a circle sentencing court for a new penalty
b.why: Parole depends on following conditions. When it is revoked, the person may return to prison to serve more of the sentence. The sentence had not ended, so it cannot be treated as finished.
b.clue: Parole is a release on conditions, not the end of the sentence.

a.best: They serve part of the sentence under community supervision

b.best: He may be returned to prison to serve more of the sentence

problems.detail: 'In NSW, the State Parole Authority decides whether a prisoner is released on parole' is overgeneralised. For sentences of three years or less with a non-parole period, the court makes a parole order and release is automatic at the end of the non-parole period. The State Parole Authority decides release mainly for sentences over three years. It also revokes parole for all parolees.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may be returned'). The other three are flat, absolute claims, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Post-sentencing
card: Parole
Parole lets a prisoner serve the last part of a sentence in the community, under supervision. It is a release on conditions, and the sentence has not ended.
Conditions
A parolee must follow set conditions, such as reporting to a supervising officer. If they break the conditions, the State Parole Authority can revoke parole and return them to prison.
Parole decisions

The court sets the non-parole period, the minimum time to serve in custody. In NSW, for sentences of three years or less, the court's parole order usually means release once it ends. For longer sentences, the State Parole Authority decides.
After the sentence

b.q: Sam is on parole. He stops reporting to his supervising officer, and the State Parole Authority revokes his parole. What happens next?
opts: He goes back to prison to serve more of his sentence
His conviction is quashed because supervision was unfair
His sentence ends because he was already released
He is given a new, longer sentence for the original crime
b.why: Parole is a release on conditions while the sentence is still running. When it is revoked, Sam returns to prison to serve more of that same sentence. His sentence has not ended, and revoking parole does not add a new sentence.
